title: ⚔️ Boss: tenses and degrees in one story

questions.prompt:
A school magazine describes Mr Hamadi's bakery. Complete the sentence.

"Every morning, Mr Hamadi (open) ___ his bakery at five o'clock."
questions.explanation: "Every morning" shows a habit, so the verb is in the present simple. Mr Hamadi is one person (he), so the verb takes its -s. The continuous is for an action happening now, and the past form belongs to a finished time.

questions.prompt:
A school magazine describes Mr Hamadi's bakery. Complete the sentence.

"The crust of the new loaf is (thin) ___ the crust of the old one."
questions.explanation: Thin is a short adjective, so the comparison takes -er, and the last consonant doubles after one vowel and one consonant. Two crusts are compared, so the sentence needs "than" before the second one.

questions.prompt:
A school magazine describes Mr Hamadi's bakery. Complete the sentence.

"His grandfather (build) ___ the first oven of the bakery in 1962."
questions.explanation: "In 1962" is a finished time, so the verb is in the simple past. Build is irregular: its past form is not made with -ed.

questions.prompt:
A school magazine describes Mr Hamadi's bakery. Complete the sentence.

"Recently, Mr Hamadi (hire) ___ two young bakers."
questions.explanation: "Recently" gives no finished time and links the action to today, so the verb is in the present perfect: have or has, then the past participle. Mr Hamadi is one person (he), so the auxiliary is "has", and the regular verb hire takes -d.

questions.prompt:
A school magazine describes Mr Hamadi's bakery. Complete the sentence.

"Of all the ovens in the street, Mr Hamadi's is (old) ___ ."
questions.explanation: "Of all the ovens" puts one oven at the top of a group, so the superlative is needed, and it always has "the" in front of it. Old is a short adjective: it takes -est, not "most".

questions.prompt:
A school magazine describes Mr Hamadi's bakery. Complete the sentence.

"Mr Hamadi (open) ___ his bakery in 2015, and lately he (sell) ___ bread to many tourists."
questions.explanation: "In 2015" is a finished time, so the first verb is in the simple past. "Lately" links the action to today with no finished time, so the second verb is in the present perfect: has, then the past participle of sell.

questions.prompt:
A school magazine describes Mr Hamadi's bakery. Complete the sentence.

"Before 2015, the street (have) ___ five bakeries. Today, Mr Hamadi's is (popular) ___ of them all." Choose the correct pair.
questions.explanation: "Before 2015" is a finished time, so the first verb is in the simple past. "Of them all" puts one bakery at the top of a group, so the superlative is needed, with "the" in front of it. Popular is a long adjective: it takes "the most", not -est.

questions.prompt:
A school magazine describes Mr Hamadi's bakery. Complete the sentence.

Which sentences are correct?

options.text: Mr Hamadi's niece helps in the bakery every Saturday.
The bakery has won a prize in 2019.
His loaves are more expensive than the loaves at the supermarket.
Of all our bakers, Mr Hamadi is more patient.
Yesterday, a journalist has visited the shop.
The bakery has just opened a second shop.

questions.explanation: The habit with "every Saturday" takes the present simple with its -s; two kinds of loaf compared take "more ... than"; "just" goes with the present perfect. The others break a rule: a present perfect cannot take a finished time such as 2019 or yesterday, and a comparison with a whole group ("Of all our bakers") needs the superlative, not "more" alone.
